109: Customs classification of imported L-carnitine products (L-Tauro and GlycoCarn) under HTSUS heading 2936 (vitamins) rather than heading 2923 (quaternary ammonium salts); court held carnitine is prima facie classifiable as a vitamin because it is essential for neonates.

We hold that carnitine, and Sigma-Tau's products, are properly classified as a vitamin under HTSUS heading 2936, in residual subheading 2936.29.50, rather than as a quaternary ammonium salt under HTSUS heading 2923.
472: Classification of imported elfa top tracks and hanging standards under HTSUS heading 9403 (parts of unit furniture) rather than heading 8302 (base metal mountings and fittings suitable for furniture).
Because we conclude that the subject imports should instead be classified under HTSUS subheading 9403.90.80 as parts of unit furniture, we reverse and remand.
2566: Customs classification (HTSUS): whether bauxite proppants fall under Heading 6909/6914 (government) or Heading 2606 (importer); court held proppants outside 6909 and 6914 and within 2606.
2567: Whether the subject merchandise is classifiable under Heading 2606 (aluminum ores and concentrates), including Note 2 criteria on metallurgical use and normal processing; court affirmed classification under 2606.
The subject bauxite proppants meet each criterion.
2736: Customs classification of liquid-filled glass bulbs: the bulbs are excluded from Chapter 84 under Note 1(c) and the EN exceptions, and are properly classified under heading 7020 (other articles of glass) rather than 8424 or 8419.90.10.
we conclude that the bulbs are excluded from Chapter 84 and are properly classifiable under Heading 7020 of the HTSUS.
3527: Customs classification under HTSUS: whether the Commuter and Defender Series phone cases are 'similar containers' under heading 4202 or instead 'other articles of plastics' under heading 3926 (subheading 3926.90.99).
We affirm the judgment of the Court of International Trade in which the court classified the subject merchandise imported by OtterBox under subheading 3926.90.9980 of the HTSUS.
3848: Customs classification (HTSUS): whether GRK's imported screws are classified as self-tapping screws under subheading 7318.14.10 (importer's heading) or as other wood screws under 7318.12.00 (government's heading).
we affirm the judgment of the Court of International Trade that GRK's three imported screws are properly classified as "self-tapping screws" under HTSUS 7318.14.10.
4257: Whether imported motorhomes converted in Canada from U.S.-exported Sprinter vans qualify for favorable treatment under HTSUS 9802.00.50 and 19 C.F.R. 181.64, so as to be classified there rather than under 8703.33.00; court held the conversion created a commercially different good, so the government's heading applies.

We conclude that Pleasure-Way's motorhomes flunk a necessary requirement for favorable duty treatment under 19 C.F.R. § 181.64 and, therefore, are not properly classifiable under subheading 9802.00.50 of the HTSUS.
4699: Whether the graduated compression hosiery is entitled to duty-free classification under HTSUS 9817.00.96 as articles specially designed for physically handicapped persons, or is properly classified under heading 6115 at the dutiable rate; the court held the merchandise is not specially designed for any class of persons and is not classifiable under heading 9817.
We therefore affirm the Court of International Trade's ultimate holding that the subject merchandise is not classifiable under HTSUS subheading 9817.00.96.
5074: Customs classification of Transit Connect 6/7 vehicles: the court held the merchandise is not classifiable under HTSUS Heading 8703 and is properly classified under Heading 8704 (government's heading), after finding the CIT erred by not considering intended use.
We agree with the Government that the CIT erred in classifying the subject merchandise under HTSUS Heading 8703.
5476: Classification of imported LED decorative candles: whether they fall under HTSUS heading 9405 (lamps, not elsewhere specified) or heading 8543 / subheading 8543.70.70 (electric luminescent lamps). Court affirmed the Trade Court's classification under 9405.40.80, the government's heading.
We agree with the Trade Court's classification, and, accordingly, affirm.
5480: Correct HTSUS tariff classification of imported in-shell sunflower seeds: whether the goods fall under heading 1206 (sunflower seeds) or heading 2008 (prepared or preserved nuts and seeds), resolved under GRI 3(a) in favor of heading 2008 and subheading 2008.19.90.
We conclude that the subject merchandise properly is classified under HTSUS Subheading 2008.19.90.
6464: Customs classification (HTSUS): whether fiber optic value added modules are classifiable under heading 9013 (optical appliances/instruments) rather than heading 8517; court held heading 9013 and subheading 9013.80.90 correct.
We conclude that HTSUS Subheading 9013.80.90 is the appropriate classification for the subject merchandise.
6484: Tariff classification of imported sausage casings: whether the casings are 'completely embedded in plastics' under HTSUS Chapter 59 Note 2(a)(3), placing them in Chapter 63 subheading 6307.90.98 (government's heading) rather than Chapter 39 subheading 3917.39.0050 (importer's heading).

We conclude that Kalle's NaloProtex G1 and G2 casings are not "completely embedded in plastics" as that phrase is used in HTSUS Chapter 59 Note 2(a)(3). Accordingly, we affirm the Trade Court's decision to classify the casings under HTSUS subheading 6307.90.98.
6690: Classification of the Santa Suit jacket: the court held it falls under HTSUS 6110.30.30 (wearing apparel, chapter 61) rather than as a duty-free festive article in chapter 95, affirming the CIT and the government's position.
we hold that heading 6110 covers the Santa Suit jacket under the rule of ejusdem generis because the jacket shares the essential characteristics of the articles named in the heading.
6691: Classification of the Santa Suit pants under HTSUS 6103.43.15 (chapter 61 wearing apparel) rather than as a festive article in chapter 95.
Thus, the CIT correctly found that the proper classification for the pants is under HTSUS heading 6103, which excludes them from classification as "festive articles."
6692: Classification of the Santa Suit gloves under HTSUS 6116.93.94 (knitted gloves, excluded from chapter 95 by Note 1(u)).
Therefore, the CIT correctly found that the proper classification for the gloves is under HTSUS heading 6116, which excludes them from classification as "festive articles."
6693: Classification of the toy sack under heading 4202 (travel, sports and similar bags), excluded from chapter 95 by Note 1(d), with the court's conclusion that the classification is 4209.92.30.
Thus, the CIT correctly found the proper classification for the toy sack is under heading 4202, which excludes it from classification as a "festive article."
7065: Customs classification: whether the iPad 2 Smart Cover is excluded from HTSUS Heading 8473 as a 'cover,' including whether Explanatory Note 84.73's stands proviso creates an exception for hybrid cover-stands. Court held the cover exclusion applies, so Heading 8473 (importer's claimed heading) is rejected.
Accordingly, Apple's Smart Cover is expressly excluded from the scope of HTSUS Heading 8473.
7066: Customs classification: whether the plastic Smart Cover is properly classified under HTSUS Heading 3926 (government's heading) via GRI 3(b) essential character, rather than Heading 6307 as originally liquidated. Court affirmed classification under 3926.90.99.
The Smart Cover therefore, is properly classified under HTSUS Heading 3926.
7071: Customs classification under HTSUS: whether imported ceramic plates, mugs, gravy boats, crystal flutes, punch bowls and hurricane lamps fall within duty-free subheading 9817.95.01 (festive religious or cultural ritual articles) or the classified subheadings, held not within 9817.95.01.
we affirm the trial court's decisions to deny WWRD's motion for summary judgment, and to grant the Government's cross-motion.
7134: Correct HTSUS classification of imported Defiant-brand entry doorknobsets: the court held the articles prima facie classifiable under both heading 8301 (locks) and heading 8302 (fittings), so GRI 3(b) composite-goods analysis governs, vacating the Trade Court's classification under 8301 and remanding to determine essential character.

We conclude that the products are prima facie classifiable under both headings and that the case must be resolved by resort to GRI 3, which deals with articles that are classifiable under two or more headings.
7137: Correct HTSUS classification of imported hand tools: the court held the locking pliers are classified as pliers under 8203.20.6030 rather than wrenches under 8204.12.00, affirming the Trade Court's construction of both tariff terms.
We agree with Irwin and the Trade Court that Irwin's tools are properly classified as pliers under heading 8203.20.6030 and that the term pliers is not defined by use.
7312: Customs classification (HTSUS): whether ATBS is an amide (subheading 2924.19.11) or an amide derivative (subheading 2924.19.80); court held ATBS is not an amide and falls under the 'Other' subheading.
7649: Customs classification under HTSUS subheading 1604.14.10: whether tuna salad products are 'not minced' (threshold question under heading 1604), and whether they are 'in oil' under Chapter 16 Additional U.S. Note 1.
We hold that the tuna salad products at issue are properly classified under subheading 1604.14.10 of the HTSUS because they are "not minced" and are "in oil."
8207: Tariff classification of Ziploc reclosable sandwich bags under HTSUS heading 3923 (government's heading) rather than heading 3924 (importer's claimed heading), including the eo nomine versus use-provision question and the GRI 3 specificity determination.
We therefore affirm the Trade Court's determination that the sandwich bags are properly classified under HTSUS Heading 3923.
9515: Whether RKW's net wrap products are classifiable as parts of harvesting or other agricultural machinery under HTSUS headings 8433/8436 rather than as warp knit fabric under heading 6005 as classified by Customs; the court held the netwraps are not parts of such machinery and affirmed the CIT.
we hold that the Netwraps are not a part of harvesting machinery or other agricultural machinery.
10326: Classification of imported darunavir ethanolate under HTSUS subheading 2935.00.60 and its duty-free eligibility under the Pharmaceutical Appendix (Table 1, INN 'darunavir'); the court held the product was properly classified and duty-free, rejecting the Government's argument that the INN and CAS number identify only the darunavir molecule.
10642: Customs classification / country-of-origin eligibility for GSP duty-free treatment: whether Thai-manufactured cookware underwent a double substantial transformation (Torrington) so that Chinese steel discs count as Thai-produced materials; court affirmed one substantial transformation only, so duty-free denied.
The Court of International Trade did not clearly err in finding only one substantial transformation, so we affirm.
10750: Customs classification (HTSUS): gloves classified under heading 6116 (knitted gloves) rather than heading 3926 (articles of plastics), including whether Section XI Note 1(h) excludes the gloves from Section XI and whether Kalle's 'completely embedded' test applies.
Accordingly, we conclude that the subject gloves are properly classified as “Gloves . . . knitted” under heading 6116.
11337: Tariff classification of frozen fruit mixtures under HTSUS heading 0811 (fruit) rather than heading 2106 (food preparations); court held mixed fruit is fruit and mixtures are not 'preparations'
We agree that the common meaning of "fruit" describes mixed fruits, and that therefore the frozen fruit mixtures are properly classified in heading 0811.
11338: Classification of the five fruit-and-vegetable mixtures under heading 0811 via GRI 3(b) essential character (fruit predominates)
We conclude that the essential character of the fruit and vegetable mixtures is fruit, and that the five fruit and vegetable mixtures are properly classified under heading 0811.
11339: Classification of the mixtures under subheading 0811.90.80 ('Other') rather than specific subheadings; 'other' read as residual catch-all meaning none of the preceding categories
We conclude that "other" should be read as a broad, residual catch-all provision meaning "none of the preceding categories,"
12073: Customs classification of Richard Mille wrist watches under HTSUS heading 9102 rather than 9101, based on whether the sapphire crystal backs are part of a watch case not wholly of precious metal.
we hold that the synthetic sapphire crystal backs of the subject Richard Mille watches are part of the watch cases.
12561: Customs classification (HTSUS): The Trade Court sua sponte classified the imported planner as a 'diary' under subheading 4820.10.20.10. The Federal Circuit held that Mead's binding construction of 'diary' as retrospective controls, so the diary classification was error. Neither party's proposed heading was adopted, and the court remanded for the Trade Court to consider the parties' arguments.

Mead's interpretation of "diary" thus controls. And because Mead held that "[a] diary is retrospective, not prospective," whereas the Trade Court found that Blue Sky's product "is 'used to note future appointments,'" the Trade Court should not have classified Blue Sky's product as a diary.
12859: Correct HTSUS classification of imported medical foods: heading 3004 (medicaments, duty free) versus chapter 21 subheading 2106.90.99 (food preparations, non-zero duty). The court held heading 3004 applies, reading chapter 30 note 1(a) not to exclude medical foods.
We reverse the CIT's classification of the medical foods under HTSUS chapter 21 and hold that the proper classification is heading 3004.
14604: Customs classification under HTSUS: whether steel conduit with an interior coating falls under heading 8547 (importer's claimed electrical conduit heading) or heading 7306 (Customs' classification); the court held heading 8547 does not apply, so the conduit stays in heading 7306.
For the foregoing reasons, we affirm the Court of International Trade's grant of summary judgment in favor of the United States.
